In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the time-dependent effect on consumer judgment is not a simple function of the time that elapses between judgment and information acquisition, but depends on the type of judgment and the type of information.

the effect of time on consumer judgments is complex, and depends on the nature of the judgment task, the nature of information presented, and the nature of the information processing strategy used by the consumer.
the delayed judgment of a product is positively biased when the information is vivid in memory and when an inconsistency exists in the information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
delayed judgments are biased, but the direction of the bias depends on the conditions under which the judgment is made.
the time dependent bias is an effect of memory decay, and is limited to judgments that are based on memory of the original information, but are not based on the initial judgments.
delayed judgment may be biased positively when information is not vivid in memory and when it is inconsistent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time that elapses between information acquisition and judgment can affect judgment in a significant manner.
delayed judgments may not be as reliable as immediate judgments, and that they may not be consistent with the original information.
